# windows_iis_site (Resource)

Manages an IIS site on a remote Windows host via SSH and PowerShell (`WebAdministration` module: `New-Item IIS:\Sites\<name> -Bindings @()`, `Get/Set-WebConfigurationProperty`, `Set-ItemProperty IIS:\Sites\<name>`, `Remove-Website`, `Start-Website` / `Stop-Website`).

The site is always created with zero bindings: bindings are not managed here (see `windows_iis_binding`). The read-only `bindings` attribute (`protocol` plus `binding_information`) reflects the observed view so plans stay stable.

Only the attributes configured in Terraform are written; every other setting on the host is left untouched and undiffed (unconfigured attributes reflect the observed value). The runtime `state` (`Started` / `Stopped`) is enforced only when configured — except that a `Started` site with no bindings stays `Stopped` with a warning (IIS cannot run an unbound site) instead of failing.

Requires IIS on the target host: install it with the `windows_feature` resource (`Web-Server`; add `Web-Mgmt-Console` / `Web-Scripting-Tools` for the `WebAdministration` module on Server Core).

**Partial failures:** if creation fails after the site was already registered in IIS, the provider persists the observed state before reporting the error, so the resource is marked tainted. If update fails after IIS applied part of the change, the provider saves the observed partial state before reporting the error. Fix the cause and run `terraform apply` again to reconcile.

A nil state on error does not guarantee nothing was created: a failure that returns no state leaves an orphaned site that must be removed with `Remove-Website` or re-adopted with `terraform import`.

Import format: `<site name>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Manage an IIS site with zero bindings: only the configured attributes are
# written; everything else on the host is left untouched. The site stays
# Stopped (with a warning) while it has no bindings — IIS cannot run an
# unbound site — and starts once windows_iis_binding adds one.
#
# Requires IIS on the target host (WebAdministration module): install it
# with windows_feature first (Web-Server; add Web-Mgmt-Console /
# Web-Scripting-Tools for the module on Server Core).
resource "windows_feature" "iis" {
  name                     = "Web-Server"
  include_management_tools = true
}

resource "windows_directory" "web" {
  path = "C:\\inetpub\\tf-acc-site"
}

resource "windows_iis_app_pool" "web" {
  name = "web"

  depends_on = [windows_feature.iis]
}

resource "windows_iis_site" "web" {
  name             = "web"
  physical_path    = windows_directory.web.path
  application_pool = windows_iis_app_pool.web.name

  auto_start        = true
  preload_enabled   = false
  enabled_protocols = "http"

  log_enabled   = true
  log_format    = "W3C"
  log_directory = "%SystemDrive%\\inetpub\\logs\\LogFiles"

  connection_timeout_seconds = 120
  max_connections            = 0 # unlimited

  state = "Started"

  depends_on = [windows_feature.iis]

  # Bound every remote operation explicitly. Without this block each operation
  # defaults to 10 minutes; a stalled PowerShell/SSH session then surfaces a
  # timeout diagnostic instead of blocking Terraform indefinitely.
  timeouts = {
    create = "10m"
    read   = "10m"
    update = "10m"
    delete = "10m"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Site name. 1-64 characters; must not contain `/ \ [ ] : ; , ? * " < > |` and must not have leading or trailing spaces. Immutable after creation (ForceNew).
- `physical_path` (String) Physical path of the site root on the target host (e.g. `C:\inetpub\wwwroot`). The directory must already exist (manage it with `windows_directory`): references to `%SystemDrive%`-style environment variables are expanded host-side for the existence check and stored verbatim. Never created implicitly; updated in place.

### Optional

- `application_pool` (String) Application pool serving the site root. The pool must already exist (manage it with `windows_iis_app_pool`); it is never created implicitly. Updated in place.
- `auto_start` (Boolean) Whether the site starts automatically when WAS starts (`serverAutoStart`).
- `connection_timeout_seconds` (Number) Connection timeout in whole seconds (`limits.connectionTimeout`, 0 disables the timeout).
- `enabled_protocols` (String) Protocols the site root application listens on (`application[@path='/'] enabledProtocols`, e.g. `http`).
- `log_directory` (String) Directory for the site log files (`logFile.directory`, e.g. `%SystemDrive%\inetpub\logs\LogFiles`).
- `log_enabled` (Boolean) Whether IIS logging is enabled for the site (`logFile.enabled`).
- `log_format` (String) Log file format. One of `W3C`, `IIS`, `NCSA`.
- `max_connections` (Number) Maximum concurrent connections (`limits.maxConnections`; 0 means unlimited).
- `preload_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the site root application is preloaded (`application[@path='/'] preloadEnabled`).
- `site_id` (Number) Numeric site ID (1-4294967295). Immutable after creation (ForceNew). When left unconfigured, IIS allocates the lowest free ID itself.
- `state` (String) Runtime state of the site. One of `Started`, `Stopped`. Enforced only when configured (`Start-Website` / `Stop-Website`). A `Started` site with no bindings stays `Stopped` with a warning (IIS cannot run an unbound site); the diff is suppressed while the site stays unbound.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `bindings` (Attributes List) Read-only view of the site bindings (`protocol` plus `binding_information`, e.g. `*:80:example.com`). Managed by the `windows_iis_binding` resource — never written by this resource. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bindings))
- `id` (String) Resource identifier. Set to the site name.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--bindings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bindings`

Read-Only:

- `binding_information` (String) Binding information (`IP:port:hostheader`, e.g. `*:80:example.com`).
- `protocol` (String) Binding protocol (e.g. `http`, `https`).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a site by name. The live settings are adopted into state;
# unconfigured attributes reflect the observed values, and site_id stays
# managed (it is part of the identity). The bindings view is observed
# read-only (managed by windows_iis_binding).
terraform import windows_iis_site.web 'web'
```
